clue.text: Food for baby supplied by nursemaid — endless tropical fruit

parts.note: pap is soft mushy food for infants

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the nursemaid word is lopped off

parts.note: an ayah is a nursemaid or nanny in India

explanation.surface: A nanny feeds the baby mashed tropical fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims AYAH to AYA.
explanation.definitionFit: Papaya is a large orange-fleshed fruit grown in the tropics.

clue.text: Fellow's maybe bitter, cross with woman indoors?

parts.note: bitter is a type of English beer, an ale
X is the shape of a cross
and means with, together with
'er indoors is British slang for one's wife, from the TV show Minder

explanation.surface: A man perhaps sour and angry with his wife at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter' and 'cross' look like moods but are BEER and X.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's first name, so it is what a fellow may be called, an example.

clue.text: Attend to a duke's attire

parts.note: D is short for duke
dress means clothing, attire

explanation.surface: Looking after a duke's wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: To address a problem is to deal with it or turn attention to it.

clue.text: One working hard in Victorian times

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the words Victorian times

explanation.surface: A labourer toiling in the nineteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants are proverbially industrious insects, as in the fable of the ant and the grasshopper.

clue.text: Old-time theatre welcomes back Hollywood actress

indicators.note: welcomes means the theatre word takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a profession

indicators.note: back says the actress's name is read in reverse

parts.note: Mae West was a Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: An old playhouse greets a returning film star.
explanation.walkthrough: The actress is Mae West; 'back' turns her name into EAM before the theatre welcomes it, and 'Old-time' is an adjective, hence the hyphenated (5-3).
explanation.definitionFit: The era of railways and steam engines is a byword for a bygone period, so the phrase describes something old-fashioned.

clue.text: South African using street map in Belgravia

indicators.note: in places the street map inside the Belgravia letters

parts.note: Belgravia is in the London postcode district SW1, written SWI
the A-Z is the standard London street atlas

explanation.surface: A visitor from southern Africa finding the way round a smart London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Belgravia is an upmarket area of London; its SW1 postcode is read as letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swazi people come from Eswatini, formerly Swaziland, in southern Africa.

clue.text: Recreational drug made one high during trip, mainly

parts.note: E is ecstasy

indicators.note: during means the high pieces go inside the trip word

parts.note: a sally is an excursion or trip
sent, as in 'the music sent me', means made someone ecstatic
I is the numeral one

explanation.surface: Mostly, taking a party drug gave someone a high on the outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts SENTI inside SALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Essentially means basically, in the main, much like 'mainly'.

clue.text: Old woman has John beaten at end of long game

parts.note: ma is mother, an old woman in slang

indicators.note: beaten, like eggs whisked up, means the name's letters are scrambled
end of takes the final letter of long

explanation.surface: Mum defeats John at the end of a lengthy game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beaten' turns JOHN into HJON.
explanation.definitionFit: Mah-jong is a Chinese tile-based pastime for four players.

clue.text: I'm really pleased to try on topless stretchy garment

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the try word above the other

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt

indicators.note: topless takes off the first letter of the garment

parts.note: a body is a close-fitting stretchy one-piece garment

explanation.surface: Delight at being allowed to try on a revealing stretchy top.
explanation.definitionFit: Goody is a childish exclamation of delight.

clue.text: One obliged, we're told, to back archdeacon in dispute

indicators.note: to back means this piece follows behind the archdeacon

parts.note: an archdeacon is styled the Venerable, abbreviated Ven

indicators.note: we're told signals that the debtor word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a debtor is someone obliged to repay money

explanation.surface: Someone under obligation supports a senior cleric in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent DEBTOR is said like DETTA. 'to back' places it after VEN, the abbreviation of Venerable, an archdeacon's title.
explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a prolonged bitter feud, a kind of dispute.

clue.text: Train, second half of it getting left behind

indicators.note: behind puts the left letter at the back
half of takes just the front portion of the word the clue's 'it' stands for

parts.note: 'it' refers back to the train, which a child calls a choo-choo

explanation.surface: Instructions for shortening a train by leaving its rear coaches behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the train of the definition, read as a nursery choo-choo; 'half of' keeps CHOO.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to train or educate them.

clue.text: Staff includes brilliant teacher, one offering a European language

indicators.note: includes means the staffing word holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it
ace means excellent, brilliant
a don is a university teacher
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A school's staff has an outstanding tutor who offers lessons in a Continental tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' is a verb here, MAN, not a noun for employees.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedonian is the Slavic tongue spoken in North Macedonia in the Balkans.

clue.text: Cautious, taking dangerous bends

parts.note: on means taking, as in being on drugs

indicators.note: bends means the letters are twisted out of order

explanation.surface: A driver going carefully round hazardous corners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bends' looks like road curves but is the anagram signal on DANGEROUS.
explanation.definitionFit: To be watchful and alert to danger is the idiom's sense, i.e. careful.

clue.text: Crossing railway is bovine creature

indicators.note: crossing means the bovine word straddles the other piece

parts.note: an ox is the archetypal bovine animal

explanation.surface: A cow is wandering across the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: An oryx is a large straight-horned antelope, an animal of Africa and Arabia.

clue.text: Odd verse, odd verse

indicators.note: odd tells us to take the first, third, fifth and seventh letters of the opening two words

explanation.surface: A repeated complaint about a peculiar poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Odd verse' is the fodder and the second 'odd' the instruction to take its odd-numbered letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems addressed to a subject are a classic form of poetry, so they are verse.

clue.text: Most of our launches are canoe-like vessels

indicators.note: most of means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: triggers means sets off, launches

explanation.surface: Boasting that most of a fleet's launches are like canoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launches' looks like boats, but is a verb: sets off, TRIGGERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Outriggers are narrow canoes fitted with a float on a side spar for stability.

clue.text: Baby bear going without porridge in the end

indicators.note: going without means the porridge letter is dropped

parts.note: to tote is to carry, bear

indicators.note: in the end takes the last letter of porridge

explanation.surface: A Goldilocks scene: the little bear left with no porridge.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small child, an infant.

clue.text: Journalist's presentation about Republican being in the soup

parts.note: re means about, concerning

indicators.note: being in places the Republican letter inside the soup

parts.note: potage is thick soup

explanation.surface: A reporter's piece on a Republican politician in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the soup' looks like the idiom for being in trouble, but the soup is POTAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Reportage is the reporting of news, the output of a journalist.

clue.text: Like some rock and jazz music female's crazy about

indicators.note: about means the female and crazy pieces go round the jazz word

parts.note: mental is slang for mad, crazy
ragtime, or rag, is an early jazz style

explanation.surface: A woman is mad about rock and jazz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' looks musical but is geological.
explanation.definitionFit: Fragmental rock is made of broken pieces of older stone, as in breccia.

clue.text: Statue displayed in celebration meal

parts.note: a gala is a festive occasion
tea is an afternoon or evening meal

explanation.surface: A statue on show at a festive dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth, Pygmalion carved a sculpture who came to life, later named Galatea.

clue.text: Page with work by English author

indicators.note: by means the English letter sits next to the work

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A page of writing by an English author.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Pope was an eighteenth-century poet and satirist, a writer.

clue.text: Competition in which participants get through several rounds?

definitions.text: Competition in which participants get through several rounds?

parts.words: Competition in which participants get through several rounds?
parts.note: rounds are both batches of questions and drinks bought for a group, so contestants work through both at a bar quiz night

explanation.surface: A contest decided over a series of rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: A pub quiz is a British bar trivia night.
explanation.definitionFit: Bar trivia contests are split into question rounds while teams also buy rounds of drinks.

clue.text: Everyone's on time? Unbelievable!

indicators.note: on means the everyone word is attached after the time letter

parts.note: everyone is all of them; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Astonishment that everyone has turned up punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is an implausible one, so tall here means hard to believe.

clue.text: Stirred a pan with energy

parts.note: a wok is a Chinese cooking pan
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone stirred a pan briskly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stirred' looks like cooking but means roused from sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Awoke is the past tense of wake, so it means stirred from slumber.

clue.text: Food extremely sickly and dry, say, coming from east Pennsylvania location

indicators.note: in an across clue, coming from the east means read right to left

parts.note: grub is slang for food

indicators.note: extremely asks for the first and last letters of the word sickly

parts.note: TT, teetotal, means not drinking, dry
eg, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: Food that is very sickly and dry comes from a place in Pennsylvania.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from east' reverses the whole string GRUBSYTTEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Gettysburg is a borough in Pennsylvania, site of the Civil War battle.

clue.text: Will I want head on beer? Not half

definitions.text: Will I want head on beer? Not half

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the head word above the rest

parts.note: the top is the head of something

indicators.note: not half means one half of the word beer is dropped

explanation.surface: A drinker asked whether he wants a frothy pint answers 'Not half!', British for 'very much'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is a British exclamation meaning 'definitely'; it also removes BE from BEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy drinker would certainly welcome a frothy pint.

clue.text: Rebel fighter to settle out of court

indicators.note: out of means the court letters are removed

parts.note: to contract can mean to settle or agree on terms

explanation.surface: An insurgent agrees to settle a case privately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of court' is a legal phrase, but here it tells you to remove CT from CONTRACT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Contras were the US-backed rebel guerrillas of 1980s Nicaragua.

clue.text: Country girl had left university earlier

indicators.note: earlier puts the left and university pieces ahead of the girl

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
gal is a casual word for girl

explanation.surface: A country girl had dropped out of college before.
explanation.definitionFit: Portugal is a nation on the Iberian peninsula.

clue.text: Cleric given a turn

definitions.meaning: ..., short for Reverend, is a clergyman's title

explanation.surface: A clergyman is given his turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for revolution, it means one full turn, and also stands as a priest's title.

clue.text: One insists on having revolutionary left-winger identified

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the string is read backwards

parts.note: a red is a communist, a left-winger
named means identified

explanation.surface: Someone demands to have a radical leftist exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' seems to describe the left-winger but reverses REDNAMED.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who demands something is a person who insists on getting it.

clue.text: Important official namely twice brought before king

indicators.note: brought before means the two namely pieces precede the king letter

parts.note: viz and ie are two abbreviations meaning namely or that is
ie, id est, is the second abbreviation meaning namely
R stands for rex, king

explanation.surface: A dignitary is announced twice before being presented to the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A vizier was a high-ranking minister in Muslim states such as the Ottoman Empire.
